narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Tide Table"**

Each account's 5-hour window is read the way a harbour master reads a tide table: how high the water is now, where the prediction says it should be, and when the next low water comes. The system is a native macOS one. The ground is the system's own Liquid Glass and Light/Dark appearance; HaryX adds very little on top of it: one cyan for what is live, an amber and a red for pace and limits, a geometric display face for the numbers that matter, and hairline rules in place of boxes.

Density is that of an almanac rather than a dashboard of widgets. The menu bar panel (380pt wide) puts the active account first with its 5-hour percentage set large, a flat tide staff under it, and the rest of the accounts below a hairline as a fixed-column table in switch order. Type weight and size carry the hierarchy; chrome is removed wherever a rule or a column can do the job.

The dashboard window is a standard sidebar/detail split. Accounts are flat filled cards, active account first and then in switch order, that repeat the panel's tide reading at a smaller scale (percentage, staff with pace tick, pace delta, week staff), so the reading looks the same wherever it appears. Glass belongs to the controls and navigation that sit over this content, never to the content itself.
keyCharacteristics: System Liquid Glass for controls, navigation and floating notices; content sits on flat system fills. System Light/Dark throughout.
Electric Cyan marks the active account, live state and on-pace usage. Amber means ahead of pace or past 85%; red only at the limit.
Space Grotesk only for the wordmark, large percentages and reset clocks; SF Pro everywhere else.
Tabular figures in every number that sits in a column or updates in place.
1pt hairline rules divide sections; flat fills, no gradients, no authored shadows.

Web (site/) only: navy ground in dark, Soft White paper in light; drawn mark and full-bleed tide line as the only illustration; Space Grotesk headlines and figures, Geist text, Geist Mono for real commands; hairlines, no cards.

rules.name: The Live Cyan Rule
rules.body: Cyan means live or on pace: the active account, a running session, an enabled automation, a fill that is on pace. Do not use it for decoration or for a heading. Small live text on glass is carried by a cyan dot beside secondary text, not by cyan text.

rules.name: The Three-Step Fill Rule
rules.body: A usage reading is cyan while on pace, amber when ahead of pace or at 85% or more, red at 100%. Ahead of pace means 5 or more points over the expected pace when a pace is known, otherwise the CLI's own verdict; drift under 5 points is on pace. In almanac columns a percentage is coloured only from 85% up; below that it stays primary text.

rules.name: The Display-Only Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk appears only in the wordmark, the large percentages and the reset clocks. Labels, buttons, headings and tables stay in SF Pro.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column or refreshes in place uses tabular (monospaced) digits, so the columns do not move when the values change.

rules.name: The Glass Is Chrome Rule
rules.body: Glass is for controls, navigation and floating notices. Content (account cards and readings) sits on flat system fills, and selection is a fill change, not a ring or a glass tint. Never author shadows or gradients.

rules.name: The Navy Ground Rule (web only)
rules.body: In the dark theme the whole page ground is Midnight Navy with Soft White ink; in the light theme it is Soft White paper with Midnight Navy ink. This is a deliberate exception, for `site/` only, to the app's rule that Midnight Navy is only the mark's tile. App surfaces keep the system appearance and never use navy as a surface.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule (web)
rules.body: Cyan is the page's only accent: the tide line, the active account and the route in the tide illustration, the `$`/`>` prompt before a command, the selected OS underline, link-hover underlines, the focus ring (2px, 3px offset), and the Copy button's hover and copied fill. Amber appears only inside the tide illustration, as a staff fill and its figure. No red ships on the page.

rules.name: The Web Display Rule
rules.body: On the web, Space Grotesk carries headlines, figures, reset times and platform names, wider than the app's Display-Only Rule, which stays in force for the app. Running text, statements, buttons, the OS switch and nav stay in Geist.

rules.name: The Real Command Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for commands a visitor can run (the install lines, the `haryx …` commands beside each feature, the cswap import line) and nothing else: no mono labels, captions or decorative code.

rules.name: The Hairline, Not Card Rule
rules.body: Lists are divided by 1px rules: a strong rule at the head of a list, a light rule under each row. Nothing is boxed as a card. The only outlined element is the command field.

rules.name: The Sample Data Rule
rules.body: Any usage reading on the web is an illustration and says so on the page, next to it, in plain words.

dos: **Do** put the active account's 5-hour percentage first, as the one Display figure on the surface, with the reset clock right-aligned beside it.
**Do** draw every usage reading as a Tide Staff (flat fill, 1.5pt radius, pace tick) coloured cyan / amber / red by the Three-Step Fill Rule.
**Do** use tabular figures for every percentage, clock and countdown.
**Do** divide panel sections with 1pt system-separator rules and 10pt of space on each side.
**Do** use the system label tiers for all neutral text, keep content on flat system fills, and show selection as the accent fill at 18%.
**Do** use the navy ground in dark and Soft White paper in light on `site/`, and only there.
**Do** let the drawn mark and the tide line be the page's only illustration, with the tide line full-bleed and behind the mark.
**Do** divide every list with 1px hairlines and leave sections separated by space.
**Do** label every usage illustration as sample data, in plain words beside it.
**Do** keep the install command, with its OS switch and Copy, above the fold and repeat it at the close.
**Do** honour reduced motion: every entrance resolves to its end state, and `?still` renders that end state for captures.
donts: **Don't** set labels, buttons, headings or table text in Space Grotesk; it is reserved for the wordmark, large figures and clocks.
**Don't** use cyan for anything that is not live, active or on pace, and don't use red before a window is at its limit.
**Don't** put content on glass or add gradients and authored shadows; cards are flat system fills and glass is for controls, navigation and floating notices.
**Don't** put borders or rings on containers, including for selection; selection is the accent fill at 18%.
**Don't** draw a usage reading as a capsule progress bar or label it in uppercase; use the Tide Staff and sentence case.
**Don't** use Midnight Navy as a surface or text colour; it exists as the mark's tile.
**Don't** box content in cards, add shadows, gradients or glass, or fill a section band.
**Don't** set anything but a runnable command in Geist Mono.
**Don't** add a second accent: cyan is the only one, amber lives only inside the tide illustration.
**Don't** present a usage figure as live data.
